clue.text: Garment overweight duck put to some purpose

indicators.note: over tells the solver to turn the abbreviation for weight the other way round

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
a duck is a nought in cricket, the shape of the letter O
to put something to a purpose is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone describes a garment while musing on an overweight duck being made useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overweight' reads as one adjective, but it splits into the reversal signal 'over' and the word it acts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A blouse is a loose upper garment, usually worn by women.

clue.text: Fat one who cries

explanation.surface: A plump person bursts into tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Blubber is whale fat; to blubber is to weep noisily, so a blubberer cries.

clue.text: Rictus boy concealed in darkness

indicators.note: concealed suggests the letters are disguised by being rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy's grimace is lost in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: A rictus is a fixed grin or grimace.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscurity is dimness or a lack of light.

clue.text: Throw out peculiar cloth

indicators.note: out says the throw is placed on the outside of the other word

parts.note: to shy is to throw
odd means peculiar

explanation.surface: Someone discards strange fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw out' reads as discard; 'out' is the container signal, putting the throw around the peculiar part.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy is a cheap cloth made from recycled wool.

clue.text: Perfect novice has to enter to seek for prize

indicators.note: has to enter means the novice's letter is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: to compete is to try to win a prize
L is a learner, the L-plate of a novice driver

explanation.surface: A beginner is told to join a contest for a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: L (learner) goes inside COMPETE after its P. 'Perfect' is an adjective here: a complete set is a perfect one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something complete lacks nothing, which is what perfect means as an adjective.

clue.text: Formerly to be found in London cemetery

indicators.note: to be found in means the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: Something old used to lie in a London graveyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past.

clue.text: Forbearance shown by a model — one without money

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the money goes round the other pieces

parts.note: pence are money
the Model T Ford makes T stand for model
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A penniless model shows great forbearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking; here it means outside, PENCE around A, T, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is calm endurance.

clue.text: Partly perceive the result in the clear upper air

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone half-sees an outcome up in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took 'in' as well; 'in the clear upper air' cannot replace a noun, so 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was the old poetic name for the pure upper sky.

clue.text: Finish rose-plot at back

parts.note: an end is a finish

indicators.note: plot as a verb suggests rearranging, as in plotting a new layout

explanation.surface: A gardener completes a rose bed at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a garden bed; it rearranges ROSE into ORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a plan is to support it.

clue.text: Outcome of lofted drive

parts.note: a lofted ball goes up
a drive is a shot in cricket or golf

explanation.surface: A golfer or batsman considers what happens after a ball is hit high.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot of an affair is its final result.

clue.text: Drink journalist takes when frustrated

parts.note: Scotch whisky is a drink
ED is short for editor, the senior journalist

explanation.surface: A thwarted reporter turns to the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' just joins the drink to the journalist; ED is the usual crossword editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that is scotched has been stopped or thwarted.

clue.text: Excursionist making a slip

explanation.surface: A day-tripper stumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is someone on an outing; one who trips makes a slip.

clue.text: 4 perhaps or 6 — that is the limit!

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator exclaims over a big hit.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball reaching the edge of the field scores four, or six if it lands beyond it without bouncing.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a hit to the rope scores four or six runs; generally the word means an edge or limit.

clue.text: Fear of mistake by model

parts.note: the Model T was the early Ford car, so T stands for model
an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: An anxious model dreads making a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme dread.

clue.text: Mad French caper

parts.note: an antic is a playful caper

explanation.surface: A wild French prank.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means wildly agitated.

clue.text: Check precipitation in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the word for precipitation is heard, not written

parts.note: rain is the commonest precipitation

explanation.surface: A forecaster mentions rain, or so it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse or a habit is to restrain it.

clue.text: Show full awareness of rise in value

explanation.surface: An investor understands that an asset is gaining worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate something is to recognise its worth fully; an asset that appreciates gains in value.

clue.text: Amount allocated for plot to be cultivated

explanation.surface: A gardener is given a share of land.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an allotment is a small rented plot for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a share handed out, and in Britain a rented garden plot.

clue.text: Leading Dutch artist embracing one in absent-minded fashion

indicators.note: Leading means just the opening letter of the word is taken
embracing means the numeral for one goes inside the word artist
fashion as a verb means to shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Dutch painter is lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: D, then ARTIST with I inside rearranged as ISTRAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrait means distracted or preoccupied.

clue.text: Where one may find shelter in windy sea?

annotationWithheld.why: 'Where one may find shelter in windy sea? (7,3)': the letters of IN WINDY SEA make WAYSIDE INN (grid prints WAYSIDEING), but 'windy' must be both fodder and the anagram signal
annotationWithheld.clue: Where one may find shelter in windy sea?

clue.text: Fish of size

annotationWithheld.why: 'Fish of size (7)': whiting is the fish, but no sense of 'size' gives WHITING and the scan shows no more text

clue.text: Expression of grief a girl uttered

indicators.note: uttered says the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl cries out in sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Alas' is an interjection of sorrow.

clue.text: Calls emitted by Sunday hikers?

indicators.note: emitted suggests the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Walkers out on a Sunday make loud cries.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrieks are shrill cries.

clue.text: Got to know humorist by book

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote comic nonsense verse
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone learned about a comic writer from a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To have learnt something is to have come to know it.

clue.text: Some find it easy to compose

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer claims composing comes naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: To indite a letter or poem is to write it, an old word for composing.

clue.text: Hurry on stroke

explanation.surface: A golfer is urged on to the next shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive is to urge forward; a drive is a long shot in golf or cricket.

clue.text: Father confessor to the film industry?

definitions.text: Father confessor to the film industry?

parts.words: Father confessor to the film industry?
parts.note: a priest who hears confessions is a spiritual guide, and the person who guides a film shares that title

explanation.walkthrough: A spiritual director is a priest who guides a penitent; a film director guides a film.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a priest who guides souls and the person in charge of making a film.

clue.text: Bird responsible for revolution it is said

indicators.note: it is said tells the solver the word is heard aloud

parts.note: a turn is one revolution

explanation.surface: A bird is blamed for a rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tern is a seabird.

clue.text: No loss from meditation being copied

indicators.note: loss from says the letters of No are taken out of the longer word, the rest then rearranged

explanation.surface: Losing nothing through meditation is copied by others.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N and O out of MEDITATION and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imitated has been copied.

clue.text: Disturbance caused by gadfly

explanation.surface: A horse is upset by a biting fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breeze' is an old word for a gadfly, and colloquially a quarrel or row.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is a squabble or row, and in old usage a horsefly.

clue.text: Salutation bringing tears to Scotland

explanation.surface: A welcome so moving it makes a Scot weep.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots, 'greet' means to weep, so greeting there is crying.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting is a word of welcome; in Scots 'greeting' means weeping.

clue.text: Sets forth conditions

explanation.surface: A contract lays out its terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To state is to declare; states are conditions or situations.
